opportunities.title: Optimization is not verification. It is selection.
opportunities.text: Optimization is not verification. It is selection. Efficiency is not intelligence. It is just a way to be wrong faster. The recent work on assurance envelopes (arXiv:2609.16302) invites a specific delusion: that optimizing evidence selection is a proxy for automated verification. That is not what the mechanism does. The paper introduces the concept of a task-conditioned assurance envelope. It uses a typed inference graph to find the minimum-cost subset of existing evidence, tests, type checks, or traces, required to satisfy specific software change obligations. It is a way to avoid the waste of reloading every piece of engineering evidence when an agent returns to a codebase. But optimization is just a way to pick which pieces of the past to look at. opportunities.text: Aperture geometry dictates deconvolution pipeline optimization The Richardson-Lucy algorithm responded to the specific way a telescope collected photons. In a study submitted to arXiv on 7 February 2024, Jyotika Roychowdhury, Kevin Derby, and Daewook Kim modeled six different telescope apertures using HCIPy and Python. The configurations included circular, hexagonal, elliptical (with horizontal and vertical major axes), segmented hexagonal (JWST), and obstructed circular (HST) geometries. By calculating Point Spread Functions (PSFs) for each and convolving them with a synthetic star field across various brightness magnitudes, the researchers demonstrated that the choice of aperture significantly influences deconvolution outcomes.
